slides.say: In a certain season, a basketball team won thirty percent of its first forty games. From the forty-first game on, the team won all of its games until the end of the season. Because of that, its overall winning percentage rose to fifty percent. How many games in total did the team win in this season?
At first it won thirty percent of its games, and in the end, fifty percent. Let's see what that means in games.
at: At first it won thirty percent

slides.say: We haven't learned percents yet, so here's what we need. Ten percent means a tenth. A tenth of forty games is four games. Thirty percent is three tenths. So thirty percent is three times four, twelve games.
So it won twelve of the first forty games, and it lost all the rest. Forty minus twelve is twenty-eight losses.
From game forty-one, the team only wins. No more losses at all. So the number of losses stays twenty-eight until the end of the season.
Until when does it keep winning? Fifty percent is half. So in the end, exactly half of the games are wins, and half are losses. That means the number of wins equals the number of losses.
at: That means the number of wins

slides.say: So it wins the next game, and the next one, and the next, until it has as many wins as losses. The losses are twenty-eight, so in the end it has twenty-eight wins.
at: until it has as many wins as losses

slides.say: Careful with choice number three, twenty. That's half of forty, but the season didn't stop at forty games. It went on until the wins caught up with the losses. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides: This question comes at the end of the section, and it's solved in seconds, with almost no calculation. The key to understanding it is that the number of losses stays the same. It won twelve and lost twenty-eight, so it needs to reach twenty-eight wins.
